messages:
zara: hey team, new hire here. followed the README and `docker-compose up db` but the container fails to bind port 5432: `Bind for 0.0.0.0:5432 failed: port is already allocated`. I don't have any other docker containers running. wtf?

 tom: welcome! simplest cause: you probably have Postgres running on your host (system postgres) already listening on 5432. run `ss -ltnp | grep 5432` or `lsof -i :5432` to see.

 zara: yep `sudo ss -ltnp | grep 5432` shows `LISTEN 0.0.0.0:5432  pid=1234/postgres` that's the distro default postgres. didn't think of that.

 rachel: common on linux dev boxes. two quick fixes: 1) stop the host postgres (`sudo systemctl stop postgresql`) while you use the docker one, or 2) change your compose port mapping to something like `- \"15432:5432\"` and update your app `DATABASE_URL` to use port 15432.

 zara: stopped systemd postgres and `docker-compose up` works now. app still expects 5432 though (env in .env). is it better to change the app or stop the host service?

 tom: for short-term dev either is fine. long-term we prefer app config so you can run both side-by-side (e.g., host postgres for local tooling and container for the app or vice versa). if multiple people in the team use 15432, add it to the README to avoid collisions.

 rachel: small note: if you set `network_mode: host` in compose, the container will share host network and you won't get port mapping; but that is not portable on mac/docker desktop (and not recommended for people on shared infra). Stick with normal bridge networking and explicit port mappings.

 zara: curious: are there any gotchas with pg socket files? i remember something about unix sockets taking precedence over TCP?

 tom: yespsql by default tries unix domain socket first if you do `psql -h localhost` it uses TCP; if you do `psql -h /var/run/postgresql` it uses socket. If the host has a socket at `/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432`, local clients may connect to host postgres even if docker's port is different. Always check which host you're talking to. `psql -h localhost -p 15432` forces TCP to the mapped port.

 infra-bot: note: team convention: prefer using service names when both app+db run in compose (e.g., `db:5432`) and reserve host port 5432 only if you need host tools to connect. See handbook: /handbook/dev/local-db-port-policy.

 devex-bot: pro tip: add a `.env.example` with `DB_PORT=15432` and a small script `scripts/start-local.sh` that exports env and runs compose to reduce confusion for new hires.

 zara: thanks all! stopping host postgres fixed my immediate problem. i'll add the 15432 note to my onboarding doc so others don't trip on this. :raised_hands:
